title: Why You See Mirages in the Desert
hook: Desert travellers sometimes see an oasis, but it is not there.

narration.text: Desert travellers sometimes see an oasis, but it is not there.
This optical illusion is called a mirage.
It happens when light bends as it passes through air layers of different temperatures.
Hot ground heats the air above it, creating a layer of much warmer, less dense air.
Light from the sky travels down and bends upwards when it hits this hot air.
Our brains interpret this bent light as if it came from the ground itself.
This makes the sky's blue light look like a pool of water reflecting the sky.
It is a trick of light, not a hallucination.
Have you ever seen a mirage on a hot road?

description: Ever wondered why you sometimes see what looks like water in the distance when it is really hot? This video explains the science behind desert mirages. It is all about how light interacts with different air temperatures.
topic: Why you sometimes see an oasis in the desert, explaining the physics of light refraction and atmospheric conditions.
